findings.title: Optimized paginator is incompatible with datetime ordering
findings.body: The endpoint uses OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by='-datetime'. OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil on the field value and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor value, while AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime. Any non-empty optimized page will raise TypeError, and the cursor value would also be compared to a timestamp column as an integer.

findings.title: Negative offset slicing in OptimizedCursorPaginator will crash
findings.body: When enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset is negative, OptimizedCursorPaginator slices the queryset with a negative start offset and possibly a negative stop offset. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing, so this raises AssertionError. Since cursor offsets come from client-provided cursor strings and the audit-log endpoint enables advanced features, an authorized user can trigger a 500.

findings.title: BasePaginator now passes negative prev offsets to QuerySet slicing
findings.body: The new start_offset logic uses cursor.offset directly when cursor.is_prev is true. If a client supplies a negative offset in a previous-page cursor, the queryset is sliced with a negative offset. Django QuerySets do not support negative offsets, so this raises AssertionError. This affects all BasePaginator subclasses, including DateTimePaginator.

findings.title: Typo prevents reversing queryset ordering for previous pages
findings.body: In BasePaginator.build_queryset, when converting an existing '-key' ordering to ascending for a previous page, the code assigns to queryset.query.order_b instead of queryset.query.order_by. The queryset ordering is therefore not changed, so previous-page pagination can query with the wrong ORDER BY and return incorrect results. This affects paginators built on BasePaginator, including the new OptimizedCursorPaginator.

findings.title: Changing span-buf:s:* keys from sets to sorted sets is not migration-safe
findings.body: The PR changes span buffer keys from Redis sets (SADD/SCARD/SSCAN) to sorted sets (ZADD/ZCARD/ZSCAN) while keeping the same key names. Existing in-flight keys written by the old code can remain for up to redis_ttl, default 3600 seconds. New ZADD/ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZSCAN operations on those set-typed keys will return WRONGTYPE errors, causing span buffering and flushing failures during rollout.

findings.title: Silent eviction can drop spans, including root spans, and ignores configured limits
findings.body: The Lua script uses ZPOPMIN to remove the lowest-scored members whenever a segment has more than 1000 spans. This silently discards spans, can evict the root/segment span while leaving the has_root_span flag set, and bypasses the Python max_segment_spans configuration. There is no metric or log, so incomplete segments can be produced without observability.

findings.title: ZUNIONSTORE default SUM can corrupt span scores
findings.body: The Lua script uses ZUNIONSTORE without specifying AGGREGATE. If the same span payload/member exists in both source sorted sets, Redis sums the end_timestamp_precise scores. The corrupted score changes eviction order and can prevent the span from being evicted when expected. An explicit AGGREGATE MAX or MIN should be used.

findings.title: max_segment_spans parameter is now ignored
findings.body: SpansBuffer still accepts and stores max_segment_spans, but the new Lua script hardcodes the cap at 1000 and the Python flush path no longer enforces max_segment_spans. Callers configuring this parameter will get a different silent limit and a behavior change from skipping oversized segments to evicting spans.

findings.title: Consumer assumes end_timestamp_precise is present and valid
findings.body: process_batch indexes val['end_timestamp_precise'] and passes it directly to Redis ZADD as a score. If a message lacks the field, has null, or has a non-numeric value, the consumer raises KeyError/TypeError and processing stops. Since this field is newly required by the buffer, invalid or older messages need validation or a safe fallback.

findings.title: Redirect-chain limit reduced to 1000 may split deep traces
findings.body: The redirect resolution loop was lowered from 10000 to 1000. If a redirect chain is longer than 1000, the script stops early and maps the span to an intermediate set, which can prevent related spans from being merged into the same segment. This trades correctness for bounded runtime and should be documented or metered.

findings.title: No tests cover eviction, large segments, or sorted-set migration
findings.body: The updated tests only add end_timestamp_precise to small segments. They do not create more than 1000 spans, do not verify which spans are evicted by score, do not test duplicate-member ZUNIONSTORE behavior, and do not cover interaction with old set-typed keys. Given the new data-dropping behavior, this is a significant test gap.

findings.title: Optimized audit-log pagination path has no tests
findings.body: The new optimized_pagination branch and OptimizedCursorPaginator are not covered by tests. Given the datetime incompatibility and negative-offset crash paths, this endpoint/paginator combination needs explicit tests before merging.
